paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the Loss Ratio (%) as a function of computational cost measured in TFLOPs (tera floating-point operations per second), comparing different variants of the SepLLM model against a baseline "Vanilla" model. The x-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 1e7 to 9e8 TFLOPs, with tick marks at regular logarithmic intervals (1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 3e8, 4e8, 5e8, 6e8, 7e8, 8e8, 9e8). The y-axis is linear, ranging from 94% to 100% in 1% increments, labeled as "Loss Ratio (%)". Five lines are plotted: the purple line with upward-pointing triangles represents "Vanilla" and remains nearly constant at approximately 99.9% across all TFLOPs. The orange line with circles ("SepLLM (n=64)") starts at about 98.5% at 1e7 TFLOPs and increases to around 99.9% by 4e8 TFLOPs. The blue line with crosses ("SepLLM (n=128)") begins at 97% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to approximately 99.8% at 3e8 TFLOPs, and then plateaus. The green line with diamonds ("SepLLM (n=64, H)") starts at 97.3% at 1e7 TFLOPs, increases to about 99.8% at 3e8 TFLOPs, and then stabilizes. The red line with circles ("SepLLM (n=64, H/T)") begins at 94% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to about 98.8% at 5e8 TFLOPs, and then slightly declines to approximately 98.5% at 9e8 TFLOPs. All lines show an upward trend with increasing TFLOPs, except the red line which plateaus and slightly decreases at higher computational costs.
